record.paper_title: Some open problems about aspherical closed manifolds
record.context_brief: Homological growth in towers of finite covers
record.original_question: Let M be an aspherical closed manifold of dimension d with fundamental group G = π1(M), and let G = G0 ⊇ G1 ⊇ ... be a descending chain of normal subgroups of finite index with trivial intersection. Writing M[i] = Gi\M̃ for the covering corresponding to Gi and letting F be a field, do the normalized Betti numbers b_n(M[i];F) / [G : Gi] converge to the L²-Betti numbers b_p^(2)(M̃) for every p >= 0? Moreover, if 2p+1 != d, must the normalized logarithms ln(|tors(Hp(M[i]))|) / [G : Gi] converge to 0, and if d = 2p+1, must they converge to (-1)^p * ρ^(2)(M̃)?

evidence.quote:
Let M be an aspherical closed manifold of dimension d and fundamental group G = π1(M). Let G = G0 ⊇ G1 ⊇ ··· be a descending sequence of in G normal subgroups [G : Gi] with trivial intersection ⋂i≥0 Gi = {1}. Put M[i] = Gi\M̃, where M̃ is the universal covering. Let F be an field. Then
1. We get for any p ≥ 0
b(2)p(M̃) = limi→∞ bn(M[i];F) / [G : Gi];

2. We get for any natural number p with 2p+1 ≠ d
limi→∞ ln(|tors(Hp(M[i]))|) / [G : Gi] = 0,
and we get in the case d = 2p+1
limi→∞ ln(|tors(Hn(M[i]))|) / [G : Gi] = (−1)p · ρ(2)(M̃).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be an aspherical closed manifold of dimension $d$ with fundamental group $G=\pi_1(M)$, and let $\widetilde M$ denote its universal cover. Suppose
$$G=G_0\supseteq G_1\supseteq G_2\supseteq\cdots$$
is a descending chain of normal subgroups of finite index in $G$ with $\bigcap_{i\geq 0}G_i=\{1\}$. For each $i\geq 0$ let $M[i]=G_i\backslash\widetilde M$ be the finite covering of $M$ associated to $G_i$, and let $F$ be a field. Write $b_p(M[i];F)$ for the $p$-th Betti number with $F$-coefficients, $\mathrm{tors}(H_p(M[i]))$ for the torsion subgroup of the integral singular homology, $b_p^{(2)}(\widetilde M)$ for the $p$-th $L^2$-Betti number, and $\rho^{(2)}(\widetilde M)$ for the $L^2$-torsion (defined when $\widetilde M$ is $L^2$-acyclic in the appropriate sense, which is implicit in the relevant case below).

Prove or disprove:
(i) For every $p\geq 0$,
$$\lim_{i\to\infty}\frac{b_p(M[i];F)}{[G:G_i]}=b_p^{(2)}(\widetilde M).$$
(ii) For every integer $p\geq 0$ with $2p+1\neq d$,
$$\lim_{i\to\infty}\frac{\ln|\mathrm{tors}(H_p(M[i]))|}{[G:G_i]}=0,$$
and in the case $d=2p+1$,
$$\lim_{i\to\infty}\frac{\ln|\mathrm{tors}(H_p(M[i]))|}{[G:G_i]}=(-1)^p\cdot\rho^{(2)}(\widetilde M).$$
artifact.status_search_result: Part (i) for $F=\mathbb{Q}$ is Lück's approximation theorem (1994), known in considerable generality (and extended to positive characteristic in many cases by Bergeron–Linnell–Lück–Sauer and others). Part (ii), the torsion-growth conjecture relating $\ln|\mathrm{tors}\,H_p|/[G:G_i]$ to $L^2$-torsion, remains widely open; it is known only in special cases (e.g., certain locally symmetric spaces, free-by-cyclic groups, fibered cases). The conjecture is moreover incompatible with Singer's conjecture in some regimes, indicating both cannot hold in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Approximating L^2-invariants and homology growth
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic behavior of Betti numbers, minimal numbers of generators, and torsion of homology in towers of finite covers.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the framework and partial results toward the Betti and torsion approximation conjectures.

status_evidence.title: Mod p and torsion homology growth in nonpositive curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Lück's conjecture on torsion homology growth for aspherical manifolds with residually finite fundamental group along normal chains.
status_evidence.claim: The torsion part of the conjecture is established only in restricted settings and remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on L2-torsion (W. Lück)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys what is known about approximation of L^2-torsion by normalized log torsion of homology of finite covers.
status_evidence.claim: The conjectured equality with L^2-torsion in the odd-dimensional case is open in general.
